title: How Government Works
tagline: Who makes decisions, and who to go to for what.
description: A simple guide to how government is organised in Zambia — national, provincial and local — what each part does, and the rights and responsibilities you have as a citizen.
outcomes: Know the main levels of government and what they do
Understand your basic rights and responsibilities
Know which level handles which kind of concern
Feel more confident dealing with public institutions

lessons.title: Who makes the rules
lessons.body:
Government in Zambia works at different levels, and each one has a different job.

## The main levels
National government makes national laws and runs ministries like health and education. Provincial administration coordinates government work across a province. Local councils run day-to-day services in your area — markets, roads, rubbish, trading licences.

## Why levels matter
Knowing the level helps you find the right door. A pothole is usually a council matter; a national policy is not.
key_points: National government makes laws and runs ministries
Local councils run everyday local services
Knowing the level helps you find the right office
lessons.try_it: Name one service near you and guess which level handles it.

lessons.title: Your rights and responsibilities
lessons.body:
Citizens have rights, and also responsibilities that keep a community working.

## Some of your rights
You have the right to access many public services, to ask public offices for information, and to take part in decisions that affect your area. Rights come with fair treatment and dignity.

## Your responsibilities
Responsibilities include following the law, respecting others, paying fair dues like trading fees, and taking part — voting, attending meetings, and keeping your community clean and safe.
key_points: You have rights to services, information and participation
Responsibilities include following the law and paying fair dues
Taking part is both a right and a responsibility
lessons.try_it: Write one right and one responsibility that matter to you.

lessons.title: Who to go to for what
lessons.body:
Matching your concern to the right office saves time.

## Everyday matches
Markets, rubbish, drainage and trading licences — the local council. A clinic card or health service — a health facility. An NRC or birth record — the civic registration office. A local problem or to be pointed the right way — your ward councillor.

## When you are unsure
Ask at reception or ask your ward councillor. It is normal to ask — a short question saves a wasted trip.
key_points: Health facility: clinic cards and health services
Ward councillor: local problems and directions
lessons.try_it: Pick a concern and write which office you would visit first.

quiz.question: Which level usually runs everyday local services like markets and rubbish?
quiz.explanation: Local councils run day-to-day services such as markets, roads, rubbish and trading licences.

quiz.question: Taking part in meetings and voting is best described as:
options: Both a right and a responsibility
quiz.explanation: Participation is both a right you hold and a responsibility that keeps communities working.
